title: Expose the IBKR gateway's own login page URL via GET /api/ibkr/status
description:
User-requested feature (verbatim, split across two tasks): 'If ibkr is enabled, start check if user is authenticated. If not enable login button. When pressed on button, modal or browser window must open for initiating login.' The 'check if authenticated' half already exists end to end: `GET /api/ibkr/status` (backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py) already reports a `not_authenticated` state distinctly from `disabled`/`available`/`gateway_unreachable` (see `IBKRStatusResponse.state`'s own field description in backend/app/api/schemas.py), and the frontend already polls it every 30s (`useIbkrStatus`, `IbkrStatusIndicator` in the app bar) and displays a passive 'IBKR: Sign-in needed' badge (`components/common/IbkrStatusBadge`) for exactly that state. Nothing in this task changes that check.

What's missing, and what this task adds: the frontend has no way to know WHERE to actually send the user to log in. IBKR's Client Portal Gateway requires a one-time interactive browser login this app cannot automate (see `IBKRProvider`'s own module docstring) -- the gateway itself serves its own login page at its own base origin (e.g. `https://ibkr.home.arpa/` in this dev container's configuration, or `https://localhost:5000/` in IBKR's own documented default), which is a DIFFERENT URL from `Settings.ibkr_base_url` (`https://ibkr.home.arpa/v1/api`, the REST API root the app's own HTTP calls use) -- it's the same host/port but without the `/v1/api` API-root suffix, and is meant to be opened as a real page in a browser (interactive HTML form + IBKR's own 2FA flow), not called as a JSON API. This is backend-only knowledge today (`Settings.ibkr_base_url`) that the frontend has no way to derive correctly itself (hardcoding the `/v1/api` strip client-side would be fragile and duplicate backend config knowledge in the frontend).

This is the backend half: add a login-page URL to `GET /api/ibkr/status`'s response so the frontend has something safe and correct to open. The frontend half (`frontend-ibkr-login-button`, depends on this task) adds the actual button/window-opening UI.

checklist.step: Add a new field to `IBKRStatusResponse` (e.g. `login_url: str | None`) in `backend/app/api/schemas.py`, with a full `description` per CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard explaining what it is (the gateway's own interactive login page, not the REST API root) and when it's populated.

In `get_ibkr_status` (backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py), derive the login URL from `Settings.ibkr_base_url`'s own origin (strip the `/v1/api` API-root suffix -- research and confirm this is genuinely IBKR's documented convention, don't just guess the string manipulation; record what you implemented against as a `decisions` entry, the same way `resolve_conid`'s own decisions entry documents the shape it was implemented against). Decide (and record as a `decisions` entry) which `state` value(s) this field should actually be populated for -- almost certainly `not_authenticated` (there's something to log into) and probably `available` too (so a user can still reach the login page manually, e.g. to re-auth a session about to expire), but NOT `disabled` (no gateway is even configured) or `gateway_unreachable` (the derived URL wouldn't be reachable either, since no gateway process answered at all).

Full CLAUDE.md API documentation standard compliance for the changed route/schema (docstring/summary already exist on the route -- update if this changes its meaning; new field gets a `description`). Regenerate `backend/openapi.json` via `python scripts/export_openapi.py` and confirm `frontend/src/api/types.ts` stays in sync.

Tests (mocked settings/config, no live network calls per docs/architecture/Testing.md): confirm `login_url` is populated correctly for the state(s) decided above and `None` for the others, and that the URL derivation is correct for at least one non-trivial `ibkr_base_url` value (e.g. one with a non-default port, one with a path prefix if IBKR's docs suggest that's ever valid). 90%+ coverage per the project-wide gate.
